title: Tankers Burn in Hormuz Again. Last Time, America Went to War
description:
This week Iran's Revolutionary Guard reported three tankers on fire in the Strait of Hormuz. If it looks like a new crisis, it's the second chapter of an old one.

From 1984 to 1988, Iraq and Iran attacked hundreds of merchant ships in the Gulf. Kuwait put its tankers under the American flag, the US Navy escorted them through mined waters, the USS Stark was hit by Iraqi missiles, Operation Praying Mantis became the largest American naval battle since the Second World War, and the cruiser USS Vincennes shot down Iran Air Flight 655, killing all 290 people on board.

Chapters are in the progress bar.

Sources: Wikipedia, "Tanker war": https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanker_war

Pictures and footage: US Navy / Department of Defense (public domain, via Wikimedia Commons and DVIDS); Navy News This Week, 30 April 1988; President Reagan's remarks at the USS Stark memorial, 22 May 1987 (Ronald Reagan Presidential Library, public domain); Iran Air Flight 655 wreckage and mourners (IRNA, public domain via Wikimedia Commons); MV Kokuka Courageous, 2019 (VOA, public domain).
first_comment: Which moment made the war at sea impossible to stop: the Stark, the Bridgeton mine, or Praying Mantis?
